_readme: Real register rows and their dated readings, copied from the live API on 24 September 2026, for scripts/tests/project-story.test.mjs. Chosen to cover every kind of story: a MoSPI project past its date (613), a survey project whose figures fall and a press note (622), a cost that rose and a spend that fell (546), an AMRUT scheme with no readings (311), a curated record with survey readings (1), a curated record with none (2), a 0% reading (537), 100% done but still listed (518), a suspended scheme (632) and a pre-closed one (621). Do not edit a figure here to make a test pass: the point is that they are real.

project.title: Poola Subbaiah Veligonda Project
project.description: Veligonda — flood-water diversion of 43.50 TMC from the Krishna (Kollam Vagu/Srisailam foreshore) by gravity to the drought-prone, fluoride-affected uplands of Prakasam, Nellore and Kadapa districts (30 mandals); contemplated irrigation for about 4.47 lakh acres and drinking water for 15.25 lakh people. The government's own record moves backwards: SES 2017-18 says 'Overall, 81% work is completed… entire project by December 2018'; SES 2018-19 prints 74% (admin approval Rs 6,017.99 Cr, target 12/2020); SES 2020-21 and 2021-22 print 78% (target 2023); SES 2024-25 prints 75% (target 2026). Each figure is kept exactly as printed. On 1 September 2026 the Chief Minister inaugurated Phase-1 at Gantavanipalli (Prakasam), releasing water from the 18.8 km twin tunnels into the 21.8 km feeder canal towards Nallamala Sagar; press reports put Phase-1 at 19,000 acres and drinking water for about 4 lakh people, with Rs 5,662 crore spent against a project cost reported as 'over Rs 10,200 crore' (The Hans India, 1-2 Sep 2026 — press figures, no government order on record yet). The project as a whole remains ongoing.
project.department: Water Resources Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh

project.title: Polavaram Irrigation Project (Phase 1)
project.description: National multipurpose irrigation project on the Godavari near Polavaram. The Union Cabinet approved Phase-1 on 28 August 2024 for storage up to +41.15 m at Rs 30,436.95 crore, with the balance central grant limited to Rs 12,157.53 crore; the earlier approved level was +45.72 m. The estimate has been revised repeatedly: Rs 10,151.04 crore (2005-06 price level, investment clearance 25 February 2009), Rs 16,010.45 crore (2010-11 price level, revised clearance 8 May 2017), Rs 55,548.87 crore accepted by the Ministry's Advisory Committee at its 141st meeting on 11 February 2019, and Rs 47,725.74 crore recommended by the Revised Cost Committee on 17 March 2020, which the CAG recorded as still unapproved as at March 2023. Andhra Pradesh gave revised State financial concurrence for Rs 55,548.87 crore in G.O.Ms.No.21 dated 10 February 2019. The CAG performance audit put physical progress at 82 per cent for works, 67 per cent for land acquisition and 11 per cent for rehabilitation and resettlement as at March 2023, with head works at 69 per cent, the Left Main Canal at 76.05 per cent, the Right Main Canal at 96.14 per cent and the hydro-electric project at 12 per cent. Expenditure from April 2014 to March 2023 was Rs 16,089.79 crore. PIB reported Rs 18,348.84 crore incurred as at 30 November 2024 since the project was declared a National Project, Rs 15,605.96 crore reimbursed by the Centre and a further Rs 2,348 crore released on 9 October 2024. No government source publishes a single overall completion percentage for the project after March 2023.
project.department: AP Water Resources Department / Polavaram Project Authority
project.source_portal: PIB · CAG of India · Ministry of Jal Shakti · AP Government Orders

project.title: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram
project.description: Greenfield international airport at Bhogapuram, Vizianagaram district, built and operated by GMR (GVIAL) under PPP — PIB states a project cost of over ₹5,640 crore and Phase-1 capacity of about 6 million passengers a year (earlier reporting cited ~₹4,750 crore for Phase-1 works). Inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 1 August 2026; scheduled commercial operations began 17 August 2026, when all Visakhapatnam (VTZ) services transferred here — Air India's first schedules included 14 weekly Delhi flights. State records showed readiness at 98.74% in June 2026.
project.department: GMR Visakhapatnam International Airport Ltd / AP Airports Development Corporation
